- Immediate asks from your side: sample transcripts + a prioritized prompt set (you mentioned 10 typical call types).
- What we’ll deliver: short eval run (3 model candidates) with: benchmarking on your sample transcripts, prompt-set sensitivity, and streaming UX notes (partial output coherence, stop-seq tuning, tokenization effects).

Next steps: 
1) Please send the sample transcript bundle (or confirm I can use the one you dropped in today’s Dropbox).

Thanks Jordan — that looks good. A couple clarifications before you run the eval:

- Latency target: 150ms p99 is what we want for streaming first tokens, but for longer summaries we’re OK with slightly higher tail as long as partial output is coherent for users.
- Stop sequences: we have multi-line templates that should terminate on a "
### END NOTE" marker. If streaming cuts mid-marker we get odd trailing tokens.
- Data: I uploaded 12 de-identified transcripts to our shared folder and attached a short sample (.txt) to this thread.

Also curious which models you expect to be best for streaming (we’re concerned about partial-output coherence and hallucination regression when switching quantized variants).

Sam
Senior Engineering Manager, Integrations
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <spatel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit + streaming UX follow-up

Hi Sam — Marissa here (SE). I ran an initial convergence-style eval overnight against your 12 transcripts. High-level summary and recommended next steps below. Full notebook/report: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b-eval-report

Recommended model candidates (tradeoffs):
- redwood-stream-7b-v2 (FP16): best streaming coherence, low latency; slightly higher cost.
- redwood-13b-quant (4-bit): good quality, cheaper; watch for stop-sequence edge cases in streaming because of tokenization changes.
- llamax-70b-lite (quantized, server-side batching): best for complex summarization, higher latency on first token.

Findings from the quick run:
- redwood-stream-7b-v2 hit ~120ms p95 and ~180ms p99 on our 4096-token host with continuous batching; streaming chunks were coherent and respected the "### END NOTE" when configured with stop_sequences set to ["
### END NOTE"] and chunk_size of 64 tokens.
- redwood-13b-quant showed occasional partial trailing tokens when chunk_size was >128 — we recommend chunk_size 64 for streaming.
- LLM output quality (hallucination) was best controlled by an explicit finalization prompt and a short post-stream verification pass for any PHI-sensitive fields.

Attachments & artifacts I’ve uploaded/attached: prompt_sets_acme.json (prompt set we used), and the eval notebook link above.

Suggested config for POC streaming baseline:
- model: redwood-stream-7b-v2
- temperature: 0.0-0.2
- max_new_tokens: 512
- stop_sequences: ["
### END NOTE"]
- streaming_chunk_size: 64
- warmup: 3 prefix tokens (use prefix/KV cache for repeated calls)

Action items:
1) Jordan: confirm POC scope and budget estimate (token cost guidance + dedicated capacity if you want consistent p99).
2) Sam: confirm you’re OK with redwood-stream-7b-v2 as the baseline; if you prefer lower cost we’ll do 13b-quant with extra stop-seq tests.
3) I’ll run a second eval with the full 12 transcripts and share a compact rubric (precision/recall for entity preservation + a UX score for streaming coherence).

Happy to jump on a quick demo to show live streaming behavior.

–Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: prompt_sets_acme.json (JSON, 16 KB)
